Aims and Values
Our students join a global community of alumni who are empowered with the knowledge, skills and values to lead with compassion, innovate with purpose and collaborate across cultures to build a just and sustainable future for all.
We believe in achieving excellence with integrity, without compromising on individual wellbeing or our values.
Our values
Each of these aims is underpinned by our core values of aspiration, integrity, respect and engagement. It is in this way that we can ‘Work Well and Be Happy’, and truly know what that means for ourselves, and for others.
We empower students to:
At Kingston Grammar School, our mission is to live out our motto of ‘Work Well and Be Happy’, balancing achievement with wellbeing, in all that we do, throughout our lives.
We aim to equip our students with the skills and confidence they need to pursue their chosen ambitions and pathways. We understand the importance of having the right ‘currency’ in the form of examination results and other outcomes, whilst also pursuing excellence in a broad range of co-curricular endeavours as goals in themselves. We enable our students to become future-ready, able to master digital technology and to build interpersonal relationships with people from all walks of life. We also recognise that success can be different for every student and wholeheartedly aim to inspire and support each student in the pursuit of their ambitions.
We encourage and develop our students’ commitment to strong moral principles and ethical values, and to be honest with themselves and others. We aim to ensure that our students are confident in admitting when something has gone wrong and encourage them to work to find a more positive outcome, either independently or with the support and collaboration of others. This is an integral part of the educational journey at KGS and a quality that is increasingly important in a world where ‘fake news’ and sections of social media have been used to promote personal, or bespoke, agendas, which may threaten the greater good.
We hold dear the notion that every member of the KGS community should have respect for themselves, for other people and for the world in which we live whilst embracing the concept of kindness, in all its facets. We demonstrate an absolute understanding of equality and diversity, as well as promoting sustainability at every level. Beyond this, we encourage the practice of self-kindness, learning to balance competing priorities and both developing and maintaining a positive self-image.
We actively encourage our students to fully embrace all the opportunities available to them, including those they are familiar with and may well excel in, and those that are new and require a determined effort. We encourage collaboration with peers and adults both within and beyond the school, recognising how much more can be achieved when working in partnership. We invite our students to give back to the communities of which they are a part, through their leadership and service.

Welcome from our Head Master
I take great pride in being Head Master of such a happy and thriving school, and look forward to welcoming you here soon so you can see for yourself what makes Kingston Grammar School so special.
Our students’ success starts, but does not end, with their academic achievements. Our A Level and GCSE results consistently place us among the top 40 UK independent schools, opening doors to leading universities across the UK, Europe and North America.
Many students attend Russell Group universities, including Oxford, Cambridge, St Andrews and Imperial, pursuing courses such as Medicine, Engineering and PPE. Others embark on exciting journeys such as studying Economics in Stockholm, Fashion in Milan, Art at the Royal Drawing School in London or Technical Theatre at RADA.
Through a rich co-curricular programme, students explore their passions in sport, music, drama and art. We boast a remarkable sporting legacy, with students earning scholarships to institutions such as UCLA, Stanford and Yale, and produce top international athletes and Olympians.
Our strong tradition of theatre, art and music means our alumni make their mark on the stage, in performance and in all aspects of the design world.
What truly sets KGS apart, though, is our emphasis on pastoral care and community spirit. The wellbeing of each student is at the heart of all we do. Our culture of care ensures that students feel supported during challenging moments, from their first days at school to the inevitable pressures of exam season. Equally, our well-established culture of service instils in students a sense of responsibility, with all year groups engaging in meaningful community service and charitable programmes.
I take great pride in being Head Master of such a happy and thriving school, and look forward to welcoming you here soon so you can see for yourself what makes Kingston Grammar School so special.
Stephen Lehec, Head Master
Where next?

History
At the heart of the story about Kingston Grammar School stands the Lovekyn Chapel. Dating back to 1309, it is the oldest complete building in Kingston and the only remaining free-standing chantry chapel in England. Originally founded to provide prayers and masses for the soul of its founder and his family, it is today an elegant, light-filled space with outstanding acoustics, regularly used for musical performances, readings and school events. The Chapel is also available to hire for weddings and concerts.
The Chapel owes its existence to Edward Lovekyn, a prominent Kingston butcher and baker. In 1299, Lovekyn provided the wedding feast for King Edward I when he married Margaret of France. Although the King greatly enjoyed the occasion, it appears the bill was never paid. Lovekyn, who had long wished to establish a chantry chapel, seized the opportunity to approach Edward’s successor, Edward II.
In exchange for cancelling the unpaid debt, Lovekyn received a royal licence to found the Chapel of St Mary Magdalene. Built in 1309, it was endowed with sufficient funds to support a chaplain who would pray for the souls of the Lovekyn family. His son, John Lovekyn, later enriched the Chapel further and set out detailed rules for the services to be held there.
Founded by Royal Charter in 1561, Kingston Grammar School is one of the oldest schools in the country – with roots in Kingston stretching back even further to the 13th century.
Over the centuries, the fortunes of the Chapel rose and fell. William Walworth, who took over Lovekyn’s business, made substantial grants in 1371, and it is likely that boys were trained as choristers there, receiving a basic education alongside their musical duties.
This came to an abrupt end during the reign of Henry VIII. The dissolution of the monasteries brought daily worship to a halt; the warden was executed in 1540, the Chapel’s endowments were seized by the Crown, and Edward VI’s Chantries Act formally abolished chantry chapels altogether.
Remarkably, the Lovekyn Chapel itself survived.
Richard Taverner, High Sheriff of Kingston under Edward VI, received the Chapel’s endowments and may have played a key role in persuading Queen Elizabeth I to establish a grammar school in the town. When she did so in 1561, she granted the Lovekyn Chapel to the newly founded Kingston Grammar School, restoring its former endowments in the process.
The Chapel has belonged to the School ever since.
The names Lovekyn, Walworth, Taverner and Queen Elizabeth I remain woven into the fabric of KGS and are commemorated in the School’s House system, established in 1914.

GCSE curriculum
In common with many leading independent schools, we offer a combination of GCSE and International GCSE (IGCSE) qualifications. These courses are academically demanding and provide excellent preparation for A Level study, with assessment models that allow students to demonstrate depth of understanding and strong subject mastery.
Students are supported through the GCSE course with clear guidance, regular monitoring of progress and informed advice on subject choices. The option process is designed to be collaborative and thoughtful, involving students, parents and teachers, with additional guidance available for those with specific career or university aspirations.
We believe strongly in maintaining academic balance at GCSE. A broad curriculum keeps future pathways open while ensuring that students develop the transferable skills universities and employers value highly: analytical thinking, problem-solving, effective communication and intellectual curiosity.
Our students consistently achieve outstanding GCSE results, placing KGS among the top-performing schools nationally. More importantly, they leave the GCSE years confident, motivated and well-prepared for the challenges and opportunities of Sixth Form study and beyond.

Lower school curriculum
We believe firmly in the value of breadth at this stage. All students experience a full range of subjects in their first two years, ensuring a balanced education and allowing them to discover new interests and strengths. In the Third Year, students begin to make more choices, selecting a combination of subjects that reflects both their abilities and passions, while still maintaining academic breadth.
Throughout the Lower School, learning is supported by high-quality teaching, purposeful use of technology and a strong pastoral framework. Students are encouraged to take increasing responsibility for their learning, developing confidence, independence and resilience.
This carefully structured Lower School curriculum provides an excellent springboard for GCSE study, equipping students with the knowledge, skills and habits needed to thrive as they move into the Upper School.

Drama
Drama at KGS extends far beyond the classroom, with a rich calendar of productions, performances and clubs open to all students. Participation is encouraged both on stage and behind the scenes, fostering teamwork and artistic expression.
Our clubs nurture creativity at every level and give students the opportunity to explore all elements of theatre-making:
Located in The Michael Frayn Theatre, students benefit from professional-standard facilities, including fully equipped lighting, sound and staging.
We also have a flexible studio space and a green room, where students rehearse, devise and explore all aspects of theatre-making.
Whether your child dreams of taking centre stage or working behind the scenes, Drama at KGS helps them grow in confidence, creativity and collaboration.
LAMDA tuition is available for students in all year groups, from Grade 1 to Gold Award. Lessons are taught by visiting professionals and offer an excellent way to build performance confidence, communication skills and gain recognised qualifications.

Music
Music at KGS extends far beyond the classroom.
No prior experience is required to take part in music at KGS. Many students begin a new instrument or join an ensemble for the first time when they arrive, supported by specialist staff and a welcoming, inclusive culture that encourages confidence and progress.
With a wide range of ensembles, choirs and clubs, every student can find a place to develop their musical interests, build confidence and perform regularly.
Our ensembles include:
Students may join groups as soon as they feel ready. Many go on to perform in regional or national orchestras or study at junior conservatoires.
Choral singing flourishes at KGS. Our choirs include the Senior Choir, Senior Chamber Choir, Junior Choir and Junior Chamber Choir, alongside smaller ensembles and student-led harmony groups.
The KGS Choral Society, founded in 1981, brings together students, parents, staff, and friends of the School each Spring to perform major choral works. Past performances have included Verdi’s Requiem, Handel’s Messiah, and Haydn’s Creation.
We offer individual tuition on all orchestral instruments, as well as piano, voice, saxophone, guitar (acoustic, electric and bass) and drums. Lessons are taught by a team of 22 experienced visiting music teachers, and instruments are available for hire.
Performance is central to musical life at KGS. Students of all abilities are encouraged to share their music at events ranging from small informal concerts to large-scale productions.
Highlights of the year include:
We also welcome visiting professional musicians for concerts and workshops. Recent guests have included The Maggini Quartet, Roderick Williams, Voces8 and The Josephine Davies Quartet.
Our musicians enjoy regular trips to concerts and operas in London, as well as international tours. Recent destinations include Salzburg, Rome and Venice, with previous tours to Germany, Spain, Malta, the Czech Republic and France.

Venue hire
Lovekyn Chapel is one of the few free-standing chantries chapel in England and, dating back to 1309, is the oldest complete building in Kingston. Although it is no longer used for religious services, it’s the most popular venue in the Royal Borough for civil ceremonies and civil partnerships. As an elegant and bright space with excellent acoustics, it is also frequently used for musical performances and readings.
The chapel can comfortably seat 60 people. Reflecting its 14th-century medieval heritage, the room features large stained glass windows and a magnificent vaulted ceiling and arched doorway. If you want the tradition and ambience of a church but without the religious service, our chapel is the venue for you.
Hire charge: £1,500 + VAT
The Theatre (with Green Room) is the centrepiece of our magnificent Queen Elizabeth II building. It features state-of-the-art lighting, sound and special-effects technology, and a sprung wooden floor, making it an ideal setting for drama, dance and musical performances. It is also a great space for lectures, corporate presentations and seminars. The tiered seating has a flexible configuration for audiences of 176-216. The adjoining café-bar, Hawkes, is available for refreshments. Details of the technical specification for the Theatre are available upon request.
Hire charge: £1,000 + VAT

Equality, diversity and inclusion
“KGS stands for the absolute rejection of any form of prejudice or discrimination.”
This important strand of work is part of our commitment to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals – covering EDI, plus Sustainability, Wellbeing for all and promoting a culture of Service.
EDI has a considerable student input, from student-led committees, action groups and advisory panels. The Kindness Council exists to promote all four keys areas within the School, and each section has a dedicated member of staff working with them. These committed students and staff speak in assemblies, oversee displays and work with academic and co-curricular departments to promote all areas. Particular focus points in recent years have included Gender Equity, Religious Acceptance and LGBTQ+ awareness.

Learning support
If your child has a SEND diagnosis, or has been assessed by an Educational Psychologist, specialist teacher or medical professional, we ask that copies of any relevant reports are shared with the School before the start of the academic year. Where exam access arrangements have been granted at your child’s current school, evidence of these arrangements as the student’s normal way of working should also be provided.
As students progress through the school, concerns about specific learning difficulties may be referred to the Learning Support Department by teachers, parents or students themselves. Students are screened for dyslexia at key points of entry, including 11+ and 16+, using a nationally recognised screening test. Some students may also be identified through internal screening procedures during the Autumn term.
Students with a confirmed assessment indicating a Specific Learning Difficulty, or those identified through screening, may be placed on the School’s Learning Support Register and, if necessary, additional learning support may be arranged.
Support is delivered in the Learning Centre and may take place on a one-to-one basis or in small groups. Provision is focused on developing effective study skills and practical strategies that students can apply to classroom learning and homework, with an emphasis on increasing independence.
The department works closely with subject teachers, parents and, where appropriate, external professionals to ensure support is appropriate and proportionate.
The Learning Support Department works with the School’s Examinations Officer to ensure that exam access arrangements are administered fairly and in line with examination board and JCQ regulations. For external examinations, formal assessments must have been completed during the student’s secondary school career.
Students with specific learning difficulties at KGS consistently achieve strong outcomes in public examinations and progress to highly competitive universities and future pathways.
